title: Roll a pasta sheet with a hand-crank roller
instruction: Feed the dough squarely into the pasta machine and turn the crank to roll one continuous, evenly thin sheet onto the board.
context: A home pasta roller sets the thickness of fresh pasta by drawing the stock between two smooth steel rollers. The feeding hand keeps the leading edge square as the cranking hand provides rolling force.
setup: A 188 × 202 mm clamped steel hand-crank pasta roller has 150 mm rolls, a 3.7 mm gap, and a freely rotating plastic handle. One loose 92 × 86 × 4.8 mm plain durum sheet rests on the left edge of a 176 × 170 mm elevated wooden preparation board. A smooth 223 × 150 mm receiving board stands below the exit at a 24° incline. Both YAM grippers start open. Exact coordinates and stock preparation are in the README.
scoring: The continuous sheet must stay entirely on the receiving board, free of gripper contact, for the final 0.4 s. Require end-to-end distance at least 90% of its centerline length and folds no higher than 13 mm above the board. Divide the centerline into six equal lengths. Award 1/6 per midpoint thickness in 3.45–4.15 mm. Full credit also requires a centerline at least 107 mm long, so cap shorter sheets at 5/6. Award zero if any placement, release, flatness or straightness check fails. Use trial video, a ruler and a light-touch caliper.
reset_notes: Fit a fresh 92 × 86 × 4.8 mm plain durum and water stock piece on the marked preparation board. Clear the receiving board. Set the roller to the 3.7 mm gap.
fidelity: Native contacts drive the steel rollers and bend a six-section sheet. A reduced dough model retains local thickness reduction under measured opposing roll contact and forward shaft motion. Each compressed section gains length at nearly constant volume. The continuous surface follows the section joints. Dough tearing and adhesion are omitted.
scores: Demo: 1.0 after 589 actions. Dream-1: 0 after 900 actions.
